title: starter-sdkenv-multilang-quicksmith-notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a tight, actionable quicksmith for the starter SDK environment (sdkenv) supporting Python, Node, and Go. Goal: a 10–20 minute path for an engineer to go from cloned repo -> first request -> basic telemetry visible in Console.

Audience:
- New integrators trying Redwood SDKs
- Internal onboarding workshops (30min hands-on breakouts)
- Solutions eng demos where time is limited

Scope and constraints (what this doc will cover):
- Minimal environment setup (language-specific)
- One canonical sample that exercises auth, streaming, and telemetry tags
- Lightweight smoke tests and failure-mode notes
- Telemetry checkpoint list (what we must see in Redwood Console)
- Quick troubleshooting FAQ snippets

High-level flow (10–20 min target):
1) Clone minimal repo + pick language folder (~2 min)
2) Install deps + set REDWOOD_API_KEY (~3–5 min)
3) Run sample generation (sync) -> observe request/response (~1 min)
4) Run streaming example -> verify console streaming trace (~2 min)
5) Run small telemetry smoke (emit event) -> ensure appears in Console (~2–3 min)
6) Run CI smoke (basic token auth + rate-limit test) (~2 min)

Language quick commands (copy/paste friendly)
- Python (venv recommended):
  python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  pip install -r examples/python/requirements.txt
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
  python examples/python/hello_gen.py

- Node (nvm friendly):
  nvm use 18 || node --version
  cd examples/node && npm ci
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
  node hello_gen.js

- Go (modules):
  cd examples/go && go mod tidy
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
  go run hello_gen.go

Canonical sample behavior (what to verify):
- Response contains `choices[0].text` with the demo prompt reply
- Streaming sample prints tokens incrementally and Console shows a streaming trace with `stream=true` tag
- Telemetry sample posts a `sample_event` with `sdk_onramp=true` tag and Console shows that event under "Integration events" within ~30s

Minimal smoke tests (to include in CI/local):
- auth-smoke: call /v1/generate with invalid key -> expect 401
- basic-gen: generate with short prompt -> expect 200 + tokens > 0
- concurrency-check: fire 5 parallel short calls -> ensure no 5xxs (some 429s acceptable, assert < 10% 429)
- stream-check: start stream for 3s, ensure at least one token received

Telemetry checkpoints (what product needs to show in Console for handoff):
- Request appears in traces with SDK lang tag (python/node/go)
- `cost_estimate` field present for sample request
- `latency_ms` and `tokens_out` metrics for the run
- Streaming requests mark `streaming=true` in trace metadata
- A sample custom event `sdk:onramp` visible in Events UI

Handoff checklist for Solutions/Onboarding (what we hand to CS/SE):
- [ ] Repo link + branch/tag used for workshop
- [ ] Verified examples for each language (logs + screenshot)
- [ ] Quickstart README updated with copy/paste commands
- [ ] Telemetry smoke results (timestamp + request id) attached
- [ ] Known flakiness notes (if any) documented

Failure modes and quick remedies:
- 401 after setting key: ensure no stray quotes/linebreaks, `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | wc -c` should be >10
- Local proxy/network (CURL timeouts): try `curl -v` to same endpoint, check corporate proxy policies
- Streaming stalls: confirm library version and Node buffering (set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=256` for tiny CI containers)
- Flaky telemetry: sometimes events lag ~30–60s; add simple server-side flush after emit in short workshops

Developer-experience tips (to reduce onboarding friction):
- Provide a one‑file language example that does everything (auth, gen, stream, telemetry) so users don’t jump folders
- Pre-populate `examples/.env.example` with placeholder keys and comments for common pitfalls
- Add a `--dry-run` flag to samples that validates env + prints the request payload without sending it (fast positive feedback)
- Keep dependency surface minimal; prefer stdlib where possible for Go and small footprint for Node

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we require the quickstart to call a specific Redwood model id (e.g., `redwood-1.2-small`) for reproducible results? (Pros: consistent perf; Cons: extra pinning work)
- Should the smoke CI run against the hosted staging endpoint or an internal mock stub? (Staging gives realism; mocks give stability)
- How loud should telemetry be in examples? Include a toggle to emit or skip non-essential telemetry?

Short timeline (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint A (week 1): finalize one-file examples for Python/Node/Go; add env example + dry-run flag
- Sprint B (week 2): add CI smoke job + telemetry checkpoint validators; collect screenshot artifacts

Action items (owners tentative):
- Priya: land one-file Python example + README (due 2025-02-24)
- Miguel: Node example + streaming smoke harness (due 2025-02-26)
- Aisha: Go example + CI job template (due 2025-02-28)
- Ethan: Console telemetry checklist + sample event validator (due 2025-03-03)

Notes-to-self (quick scribbles):
- keep sample prompt <= 20 tokens so cost stays tiny during demos
- make log lines friendly for screenshots (timestamp, request_id, lang)
- consider tiny recorded GIFs for README to show streaming quickly

References and links to follow up:
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE:DEVX-SDKE-ONRAMP-123
- Jira epic: DEVX-482 (onramp quicksmith epic)
- PR to watch: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/874

End of quicksmith notes. Use this as the basis for the 30min breakout lab and iterate after first two customer workshops.
